title: STRAIT OF HORMUZ STRATEGIC CHOKEPOINT
subtitle: STRATEGIC GEOPOLITICS // SPECIAL INTELLIGENCE REPORT
topic: Why the Strait of Hormuz is strategically important for global energy and trade

cues.text: Across global geopolitics and maritime security,
no geographical chokepoint wields as much raw leverage
Separating the rocky shores of Iran from the Arabian Peninsula,
this strategic passage narrows to barely 21 nautical miles
Every single day, over 21 million barrels of petroleum
and liquefied natural gas traverse these waters,
accounting for more than 20 percent of total global petroleum consumption.
Under international maritime law and the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea,
yet sovereign posturing and naval mind capabilities
For the superpowers and global markets alike,
any disruption in these contested waters
would immediately trigger catastrophic global energy inflation
